executive_summary: CHF/JPY trades at 192.92537 as of the price store's 2026-09-03 close, having fallen 1.31% over one month, 3.90% over three and 5.36% over six, while remaining 3.57% higher over twelve - the entire decline is recent, and 4.46 yen of it arrived in the two sessions of 2 and 3 September alone, roughly 3.4 average daily ranges. The dominant bilateral narrative is a funding-currency rotation: the franc is now the cheaper of the two G10 funding legs at 0.00% against the Bank of Japan's 1.00%, and after the July joint yen-buying intervention the sell-side has explicitly named short CHF/JPY as the trade of choice, with ING pointing to short CHF/JPY positions as a strategy that could gain traction, 'not only because short CHF/JPY is one of the few ways to express a carry-positive yen view, but because the two currencies have similar investment characteristics'. That rotation is the bilateral signal neither standalone dossier captures: read separately, a Bearish-CHF dossier and a Bullish-JPY dossier would imply a naive collapse in the cross, whereas the bilateral lens shows that the two factors on which Switzerland dominates Japan most decisively - a 9.77%-of-GDP current account against a Japanese surplus that is 27.6 times primary income rather than trade, and AAA at 37.6% debt-to-GDP against A-band at 214.5% - are precisely what stop the tactical score clearing the neutral threshold. The settled verdict is therefore Neutral tactically (net score -0.0502, conviction 2) and Bearish strategically (net score -0.1298, conviction 2), and a short position is paid 126.9bp annualised to wait, roughly 20 pips a month at spot, which is unique among long-yen expressions in the G10. The structural map on the pair's own chart is unusually one-sided: four computed resistance zones sit within 5.52% overhead while the nearest support zone of any touch count is 179.00-179.48 at -7.09%, a 1368-pip air pocket. The principal caveat is that the base leg's rate story turned after both dossiers were built - Swiss consumer prices rose 0.8% year-on-year in August 2026, up from 0.4% in July and above a 0.5% consensus, the fastest annual pace since August 2024 - and the swaps curve now fully prices a first 25bp SNB hike to 0.25% in June 2027, which is the single most credible route to invalidating the strategic call even though it sits beyond the horizon. The second caveat is crowding: the pair-specific consensus and our strategic stance now point the same way, which reduces edge and raises squeeze risk rather than confirming the thesis.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no purchasing-power-parity model available for this cross, and neither dossier asserts one; what exists is a relative real-effective-exchange-rate comparison on the BIS broad indices for June 2026, and on that measure the gap is the widest in the G10. The Swiss real broad REER is 101.69, the 40th percentile of a cached 30-month window and down 1.03 points over twelve months, against a Japanese reading of 65.3, an estimated 2nd percentile and down 8.73 points over the same year. The 36.4-point differential mechanically implies a CHF/JPY level of 127.03 at REER parity - roughly 34% below spot - but that is a relative real gap against a 2020 base period, not a fair value, and it should be read as a magnitude constraint on how far the pair can be pushed higher rather than as a target. The honest summary is that the cross is unremarkable nominally, at the 43rd percentile of its own closing range, and extreme in real terms, with the quote currency at or near its cheapest real level of the floating-rate era. What is priced at 192.93 is a world in which the franc remains the cheaper funding leg indefinitely and Japan's real misalignment continues not to matter - the first of which has begun to be questioned by the August Swiss inflation print, and the second of which has not mattered for three years.

market_context.recent_regime: The regime is a funding-currency rotation expressing itself in a cross that had spent two years grinding higher on the widest safe-haven policy gap in the G10. Through the first half of 2026 the pair traded 198-204 with the franc winning on carry; after the 30-31 July joint Japan-US intervention - which Goldman Sachs described as 'very different' from previous rounds in both scale and coordination, estimating roughly $100bn-$110bn of action over three days, with authorities apparently intent on pushing USD/JPY below 158 and positioning remaining asymmetric - the cross broke to 193.97 on 3 August, recovered to 198.74 by 20 August, and then rolled over decisively into September. The two-session collapse of 2-3 September is the most informative recent price action, because it happened against base-leg fundamentals: Swiss August CPI printed hot the same morning and Brown Brothers Harriman noted that 'CHF is today's second best performing major currency, behind JPY'. The franc rallied and still lost, which is the cleanest available evidence that the yen leg is currently the stronger of the two havens. Underneath, low FX volatility has helped carry strategies deliver some of their strongest returns in years, but the strategy becomes more vulnerable when funding currencies experience sharp moves that erase the advantage provided by rate differentials - and a 3.4-ATR two-day move in the pair that is now the market's preferred carry-positive yen expression is exactly that kind of move.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The pair's carry is not the policy differential and must not be reported as one. The gated store's CME calendar-spread cross for 6S/6J, observed 2026-08-31 over the 13.6-to-104.7-day window, gives an annualised premium of 126.9bp, which by covered interest parity is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis and cannot be decomposed without an OIS curve. Against the bilateral policy differential of -100bp that leaves roughly 27bp of residual basis. A rolled long CHF/JPY position pays away 126.9bp a year; a short position receives it - 245 pips annualised, 20 pips per month, 19 pips over a four-week tactical horizon and 122 pips over six months. The carry regime is working against the base leg rather than for either: in a VIX-14.51 tape with high-yield spreads at 263bp, both legs are borrowed and sold, but the franc is the cheaper borrow by 100bp and the lower-volatility one, so the rotation erodes the base leg faster. Inverted, a short CHF/JPY position carries a +0.16 to +0.19 carry-to-vol ratio using the store's own estimated and corrected implied vol figures, making this the only long-yen expression in the G10 that is paid to wait, against -0.45 for AUD/JPY, -0.39 for GBP/JPY and -0.35 for USD/JPY. The regime breaks if realised volatility on the pair rises materially: a move to 12% would take the short-side carry-to-vol ratio to roughly +0.11 and make the trade uneconomic on a risk-adjusted basis without any change in rates.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is -100bp: the SNB policy rate is 0.00% and the BoJ target is 1.00%, both as of 2026-09-01 in the gated payload, making the yen the only G10 currency that pays the franc a positive policy carry. The direction of travel is against the pair and it is dated: the Bank of Japan meets on 2026-09-18 with roughly 80-90% of a 25bp move to 1.25% priced on OIS, which would take the differential to -125bp before the tactical window closes, while the Swiss National Bank's assessment six days later on 2026-09-24 is effectively certain to hold at zero because its June conditional inflation forecast of 0.6/0.6/0.7 percent is explicitly conditioned on a 0.00% rate across the whole three-year horizon. The term structure says the same thing more emphatically: on matched monthly vintages for 2026-06-01 the Swiss 10-year at 0.31% yields 236bp less than the Japanese 10-year at 2.67%, and the live JGB has moved materially higher since, though the stale Swiss leg cannot be paired with a current Japanese print. Transmission is direct and mechanical: a rolled long CHF/JPY position pays away the CME calendar-spread premium of 126.9bp annualised observed 2026-08-31, roughly 20 pips a month at the payload spot, so the pair must rise simply to stand still. The offsetting consideration, and the reason confidence is 62 rather than higher, is that the differential is small in absolute terms and the September move is already in the price.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential compresses further against the pair from one side only, because the SNB has no plausible path off zero while the BoJ has an explicit one. OIS pricing implies a Japanese policy rate of only about 1.21% after the 2026-12-18 meeting, whereas half of 36 surveyed economists now name 1.75% as terminal and 35 of 54 expect at least 1.50% by end-March 2027 - 30 to 55bp of tightening that is not in the curve and which would take the bilateral policy differential from -100bp toward -150bp or beyond. Against that, Swiss headline CPI at 0.4% and core at 0.3% remove any hiking case for the SNB, and its June forecast is conditioned on zero through 2028, so the Swiss leg is pinned with a tight and near-symmetric distribution. The dated anchors are the 2026-10-30 BoJ meeting, which carries an Outlook Report and is therefore the projection round most capable of repricing the path, and the 2026-12-18 decision where a second hike is only lightly priced; the SNB's 2026-12-10 assessment can only confirm the status quo. The genuine counterweight, which caps confidence at 66, is that the Japanese term structure is rising partly on a fiscal risk premium rather than on policy expectation, and a differential that widens for that reason does not transmit to the pair in the normal way - that mechanism is scored separately in Factor 8.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The two economies are diverging on activity and converging on nothing. Switzerland has produced the strongest surprise run in years - SECO's Q2 flash at +1.5% quarter-on-quarter against an AWP consensus of +0.2% to +0.4%, the KOF barometer at 106.7 against 103.0 expected and its highest since November 2021, and industrial production at +5.5% year-on-year against a -4.7% forecast - while Japan's Q2 real GDP grew only 0.3% quarter-on-quarter, 1.1% annualised, missing a 2.0% annualised consensus with private consumption contributing nothing for the first time in eight quarters and business investment down 1.2%. On the OECD vintages the growth differential is +2.33% against +0.55% year-on-year in the franc's favour. The inflation differential runs the other way and by a wide margin: Swiss headline 0.4% and core 0.3% against Japanese headline 1.9%, core 1.8% and a BoJ ex-special-factors measure of 2.3% that has been at or above 2% for twenty-two months. Tactically the growth-surprise term wins, because the Japanese inflation impulse is already expressed as a dated and largely priced hike in Factor 1, whereas the Swiss surprise run buys no rate change and is therefore not discounted anywhere. Asymmetric sensitivity favours the quote leg: the 17 September Japanese national CPI moves this pair harder than any Swiss release, which is why confidence is only 55.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The strategic picture inverts most of what makes the tactical read favourable and lands genuinely balanced. Switzerland's Q2 surge and record July trade surplus contain pharmaceutical exports front-running the US Section 232 regime that took effect on 31 July, with chemicals and pharmaceuticals up 25.7% in a single month, so the payback falls inside this horizon and pulls Swiss growth back toward the IMF's 0.8% for 2026 and the SNB's 'around 1%'. Japan's activity level is lower but its trajectory is not deteriorating in the same borrowed way: the corporate survey showed Q2 capital spending up 1.6% year-on-year against a 0.2% consensus with pre-tax profits up 24.6%, the composite PMI is 53.4 with new export orders at their fastest since January 2018, and the shunto delivered a third consecutive year above 5% with real wages positive for six months. On inflation the differential persists at roughly -150bp and its currency relevance runs entirely through relative policy, which Factor 1 already carries; adding it here would double-count. Netting a Swiss growth level that is good but borrowed against a Japanese growth level that is weak but improving, with the inflation channel already scored elsewhere, leaves no directional signal for the pair over one to six months.

factors.horizon_split: The stance flips from Bullish to Neutral because the tactical horizon rewards surprise flow and the strategic horizon rewards level and durability. Over four weeks Switzerland is beating consensus by wide margins and Japan is missing it, and none of that is priced. Over six months the Swiss beat is identifiable as tariff front-running that reverses, while Japanese capex, wages and export orders are improving from a low base, so the growth differential narrows and the inflation differential's only currency channel is already counted in Factor 1. Pass-2 note (does not alter the stance): the Swiss surprise run extended after the dossiers closed, and in the direction this factor already scores. Trading Economics reported on 3 September that Swiss inflation doubled in August while quarterly economic growth accelerated to its highest level in nearly five years, raising prospects of an earlier SNB hike and reducing the franc's appeal as a funding currency for carry trades. The tactical Bullish stance on this factor is therefore better supported than when it was scored - and the pair fell 1.19% on the day it was published, which is the clearest illustration in this report of why one factor at 0.18 weight does not carry a cross.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the classic low-risk-sensitivity configuration: both legs are safe havens, so the pair's beta to global risk appetite is the difference between two large and partly offsetting exposures rather than a clean directional read. The current tape is unambiguously risk-on - VIX at 14.51 on 27 August after touching a 2026 low of 14.13, US investment-grade spreads at 79bp and high-yield at 263bp near historic tights, the S&P 500 near highs and the Nikkei up 58.4% over twelve months - and in that state both the franc and the yen are borrowed and sold rather than bought. The bilateral question is which is sold harder, and the honest answer inside four weeks is that it is close: the franc is the cheaper funding leg at 0.00% and therefore the marginal borrow, but the yen carries the larger and more identified speculative short and the more extreme option skew, so a flight either way is not symmetric. One cross-asset signal is worth naming: gold, the franc's traditional correlate and the commodity Switzerland refines, is up 8.60% over a month and 22.39% over a year, which is mildly supportive of the base leg while the yen has no equivalent. Netting a cheaper funding leg against a larger short base and a supportive gold bid leaves no tactical direction.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the relative-haven question becomes directional, and it resolves against the pair for a reason that is about official reaction functions rather than about beta. If a risk event arrives, the franc's rally is explicitly truncated: the SNB stated on 18 June and reaffirmed on 8 July that it has an increased willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market to counter a rapid and excessive appreciation of the franc, and it holds CHF 889.6bn of official reserve assets to make that credible. The yen faces the opposite official posture: the Ministry of Finance bought roughly JPY 27.1trn of yen in calendar 2026, including a joint operation with the US Treasury on 31 July, and the Finance Minister has said Japan will not hesitate to conduct further joint intervention. One haven has a public official offer above it and the other has a public official bid below it, which means the yen captures more of any given haven bid than the franc does. Credit and equity volatility are close to the tight end of their post-2022 ranges, so the distribution of risk outcomes has far more room to widen than to compress, and the state in which that matters is the state in which the pair falls. Confidence is only 52 because the trigger is exogenous and undated and because both legs still weaken together in the modal risk-on path.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral tactically and Bearish strategically because the offsetting haven betas cancel over four weeks in a compressed-volatility tape, while over six months the cumulative probability of at least one risk event rises and the state-contingent payoff is asymmetric: the SNB caps the franc's rally and the Japanese official sector supports the yen's, so the pair falls in the tail even though both legs weaken in the modal path. The bilateral asymmetry this factor identifies is now explicit in market commentary rather than inferred: both currencies are treated as safe-haven assets in periods of uncertainty, but the yen fluctuates more than the franc because of interventions by the Japanese government, and the degree of geopolitical deterioration is what separates safe-haven support for the pair from a carry-trade unwind that pushes it lower.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the latent yen-buying option is larger and better identified than the latent franc-buying option, which tilts the pair lower. Japanese life-insurer currency hedge ratios are at historically low levels on both the Daiwa FY2026 survey of ten majors and a Bank of Japan Review, and Daiwa states explicitly that raising them would prompt a corresponding demand to purchase the yen; the trigger is falling hedging costs, which is a normal consequence of the base-case rate path rather than a shock. GPIF ended the June quarter with foreign equities at 25.33% against a 25% policy target, mechanically implying multi-trillion-yen foreign-asset sales to rebalance, and the reference-week securities data already shows the direction. The franc's equivalent latent bid is the -38,322 contract asset-manager short, which is real squeeze fuel but is capped in magnitude by an SNB that has said it will lean against a disorderly appreciation and has CHF 889.6bn to do it with. Add the official-flow asymmetry - a Japanese finance ministry buying yen with US Treasury participation against a Swiss central bank willing to sell francs - and the structural flow balance runs against the pair. Confidence is 55 because the hedge-ratio normalisation is undated and because the franc leg's 9.8%-of-GDP current-account surplus is a persistent offsetting bid.

Pass-2 crowding addendum: the bilateral research adds a fact that sharpens the contrarian case in the other direction from the settled stance. tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external accounts of the two economies are moving in opposite directions right now and the divergence is unusually wide. Switzerland's July trade surplus was CHF 8.1bn, the largest since the series began in January 1950, on exports up 13.8% and imports down 4.5%, with a Q1 current account of CHF 16bn or 9.77% of GDP; Japan's July trade balance was a deficit of JPY 638.3bn against JPY 156.3bn a year earlier, a 4.1-fold widening, and June produced Japan's first monthly current-account deficit in seventeen months. The mechanism is energy and it is bilateral rather than incidental: Japanese mineral fuel imports were JPY 2,680.4bn, 22.1% of all imports and up 53.5% year-on-year with crude value up 87.8% on volume up only 5.5%, so Japan's terms of trade have fallen from 90.5 in Q1 2026 to 81.62 in July. Switzerland is also a net energy importer but at a fraction of that intensity, and its franc-relevant commodity is gold, which it refines and which is up 8.60% on the month. The bilateral goods relationship is small but runs the base leg's way: Switzerland exported USD 9.3bn to Japan against USD 7.7bn imported in 2024, a net USD 1.6bn surplus. Confidence is 60 rather than higher because the Swiss July record is partly tariff front-running.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At its 0.16 strategic weight this is where the case for the pair actually lives, and the differential is structural rather than cyclical. Switzerland's surplus is the product of a goods surplus in pharmaceuticals, precision engineering and watches, a services surplus, and a primary income stream thrown off by a net international investment position of CHF 974bn, roughly 120% of GDP; Japan's surplus is 27.6 times more primary income than goods, and the goods account - the part that generates spot flow - has turned negative and is deteriorating. factors.horizon_split: Bullish on both horizons with confidence rising from 60 to 72 as the weight doubles from 0.08 to 0.16. Balance-of-payments flows are cumulative: a record monthly Swiss surplus and a widening Japanese goods deficit are curiosities over four weeks and binding constraints over six months, by which point a 9.77%-of-GDP surplus against an energy-shocked economy whose surplus is 27.6 times income rather than trade becomes the dominant structural fact in the pair.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: Switzerland is a net energy importer with low energy intensity relative to its export base, and is the world's largest gold refining hub, so gold is its principal commodity correlate. Direction: gold up is mildly franc-positive; oil and gas up are mildly franc-negative through the import bill.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Japan imports essentially all of its hydrocarbons; mineral fuels were 22.1% of July imports and rose 53.5% year-on-year on falling volumes. Direction: oil up is strongly yen-negative, LNG up is strongly yen-negative, coal up is yen-negative. Japan has no offsetting commodity export.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: yen double-negative, franc single-negative - net effect is a rising CHF/JPY because the quote leg loses more national income per unit of GDP than the base leg. LNG up: yen double-negative, franc single-negative through gas-linked power costs - net effect again a rising pair, and this is the larger channel given JKM is up 101.9% year-on-year. Gold up: franc positive through the safe-haven and refining correlation, yen neutral - net effect a rising pair. Every live commodity impulse therefore points the same way for this cross, which is unusual and is the reason the tactical weight was raised. The netting is corroborated by the observed terms-of-trade series: Japan's fell from 90.5 to 81.62 in two quarters while Switzerland posted a record trade surplus over the same window.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from the low 90s to roughly 102 adds several hundred billion yen a month to the Japanese import bill and pushes the terms-of-trade index toward the high 70s, while costing Switzerland a fraction of that as a share of GDP and lifting the gold correlate. Net: bullish CHF/JPY, asymmetric in magnitude rather than merely in sign.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent toward the low 80s repairs the Japanese terms of trade fastest because the deterioration was almost entirely price rather than volume, and removes the heaviest bearish contribution to the quote leg. Net: bearish CHF/JPY, and this is the single cleanest way the strategic bullish case for the pair breaks.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: LNG and crude jointly, transmitted through Japan's mineral fuel import bill - the Strait of Hormuz is the specific mechanism, and it matters far more for this cross than any franc-side commodity. Pass-2 wrinkle: the pickup in Swiss August inflation partly reflected higher petroleum costs and the weaker franc, with petrol prices seen 25% higher year-on-year, so the same energy impulse that drains Japanese national income is now also generating the Swiss inflation that could eventually move the SNB. The commodity channel therefore feeds both Factor 5 (pair-positive) and, with a lag, Factor 1's base leg (also pair-positive).

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Raised on both horizons: both central banks have issued unusually explicit and directionally opposed exchange-rate guidance - one asymmetric commitment against franc appreciation, one commitment to a tightening pace faster than market expectations - so the guidance channel is more informative for this cross than the default weight allows.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance divergence in this pair is as clean as it gets, because both banks have told the market things that point the same way for CHF/JPY. The SNB's 18 June assessment states that it has an increased willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market and thereby counters a rapid and excessive appreciation of the Swiss franc, language Chairman Schlegel reaffirmed on 8 July; it is explicitly one-sided, with no corresponding commitment against franc weakness and no plausible level of depreciation at which a bank forecasting 0.6% inflation would object. The Bank of Japan's communication runs the other way: the 10 August Summary of Opinions contains the formulations that the pace of policy interest rate hikes will be faster than market expectations and that it is necessary for the Bank to accelerate the pace of adjustment, the July Outlook describes CPI risks as skewed to the upside, Takata dissented in favour of a hike on 31 July, and Deputy Governor Himino called on 27 August for raising rates in a timely manner while noting that a weak yen could push up inflation faster than in the past. Layered on top, the US Treasury Secretary said publicly at the G20 on 31 August that he expects the Japanese authorities to act in ways that lead to a stronger yen. The meeting sequence matters: the BoJ speaks first on 18 September, setting the tone before the SNB on 24 September.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the reaction functions rather than the statements are what matter, and they are structurally opposed in a way that will not reverse inside the window. The BoJ's July Outlook reframed the objective from lifting inflation toward 2% to stabilising it and preventing an upward deviation, which mechanically converts every upside inflation surprise into a tightening impulse, revised FY2027 core CPI up to 2.4%, and the June decision fixed the terminal JGB purchase pace at about JPY 2trn a month from April 2027 while abolishing interim assessments - removing predictability and raising the odds of an unscheduled hawkish move. The SNB's incentive runs the other way and is reinforced rather than weakened by the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff: a central bank whose exporters have just lost competitiveness on a levy will not welcome exchange-rate appreciation on top of it, its stated tool preference is intervention rather than negative rates, and its balance sheet makes the threat credible. The dated communication points are the 2026-10-30 BoJ Outlook Report, which is the projection round most capable of moving the path, and the SNB assessments on 2026-09-24 and 2026-12-10, which can only restate a zero rate. The offset that keeps confidence at 72 is credibility: the FX market has sold the yen through an entire hiking cycle, so BoJ guidance trades at a discount, and the SNB's January 2015 precedent means its own guidance is never assumed to bind indefinitely.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish on both horizons with strategic confidence marginally higher at 72 against 70 and the weight rising from 0.09 to 0.13. Tactically there is a genuine two-sided risk in the 24 September SNB language, which could be softened after months of franc depreciation. Strategically no single point of failure exists: the BoJ's reframed objective, its upward-revised FY2027 forecast and its abolition of scheduled balance-sheet assessments compound into a systematically more hawkish reaction function, while the SNB's incentive to prefer a softer franc is reinforced by the tariff shock. Pass-2 note on the 24 September assessment: the hot August CPI raises the stakes on the SNB's language without changing the rate decision. The August print of 0.8% year-on-year came in marginally above the SNB's 0.7% Q3 2026 conditional forecast, though the July-August average of 0.6% remains a touch below it, and the next policy assessment is scheduled for September with rates expected to be on hold. A bank running marginally hot against its own forecast has less reason to keep an anti-appreciation sentence in a statement, which is the specific tactical two-sidedness this factor already flags.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The event distribution for this cross is unusually two-sided and the two large risks are close to equal in weight. Pointing the pair down is official flow: Japan bought roughly JPY 27.1trn of yen in 2026 including a joint operation with the US Treasury on 31 July, the Finance Minister has said Japan will not hesitate to conduct further joint intervention, and the US Treasury Secretary repeated the commitment publicly on 31 August - an official bid under the quote leg with no equivalent under the base leg, whose central bank has instead promised to sell into strength. Pointing the pair up is energy: US and Iranian forces exchanged fire on 30-31 August in a severely disrupted Strait of Hormuz, and any escalation hits an economy importing essentially all of its hydrocarbons far harder than one importing a fraction as much relative to output, so the terms-of-trade channel dominates the haven channel in the first instance. The dated Swiss item, the 27 September referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality, polls roughly 62% against and is most likely a non-event, though passage would force a re-examination of Switzerland's alignment with the EU and US sanctions architecture. Netting a demonstrated but short-lived official bid against a continuous energy drain leaves no tactical direction.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the event set broadens on both sides and continues to net out. The yen-positive column contains the standing joint intervention commitment with roughly USD 1trn of Japanese reserves behind it, a US political incentive to support the yen that persists at least to the November midterms, and any Taiwan or Korean escalation that would produce a classic haven bid the SNB has pre-committed to capping on its own side. The pair-positive column contains an unresolved Iran conflict past its six-month mark with a disrupted Hormuz, an unresolved US tariff on Japanese autos that are 34.1% of Japan's US-bound exports, ten months of deteriorating China-Japan relations including sanctions on 40 Japanese firms, and a Japanese fiscal calendar culminating in the FY2027 draft budget. The Swiss-specific column is smaller and mixed: the Bilaterals III ratification path is slow and probably successful, the neutrality referendum is likely rejected, and the Section 232 pharmaceutical regime is the principal Swiss-specific negative. With large identified risks of comparable magnitude on each side and no way to date the dominant one, Neutral at 50 is the honest reading rather than a failure to choose.

The composition changes - tactically the intervention option and the referendum dominate, strategically the energy and tariff channels do - but the balance does not, because in each window the largest pair-negative risk (official yen buying against an SNB that caps franc strength) is offset by the largest pair-positive one (an energy shock that transfers Japanese national income abroad). The intervention channel is the one event risk unique to this cross among franc pairs, and its scale is now documented: Goldman Sachs said the latest intervention was 'very different' from previous rounds in both scale and coordination, estimating roughly $100bn-$110bn of action over three days. The intervention threat has made short-yen positions less straightforward, and expectations of further Japanese rate increases and the possibility that GPIF could increase domestic allocations are adding to uncertainty around the currency - which is precisely the mechanism driving the rotation into franc funding.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Raised on both horizons: this is the widest sovereign-quality differential available in the G10 - AAA at roughly 37% debt-to-GDP against A-band at 214% with a live long-end repricing and a record debt-service line - and it is currently the mechanism by which a rising quote-leg yield fails to support the quote-leg currency, which makes it materially more than a background differential for this specific pair.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Japanese fiscal risk stopped being a background factor in August 2026 and became a live driver, which matters for this pair because it inverts the normal sign on the quote leg's yields. FY2027 ministry budget requests submitted on 31 August total roughly JPY 143trn with a record debt-service line of JPY 36.6trn on an assumed interest rate raised to 3.8% from 3.0%, consuming about a quarter of the request; the 10-year JGB touched 3.00% on 1 September for the first time since 1996, the 2-year reached a 31-year high of 1.743%, and the 25s30s spread is inverted at -1.0bp with the 28 August 2-year auction drawing a bid-to-cover of 2.97 against a twelve-month average of 3.74. Switzerland is the mirror image: AAA from every major agency with Morningstar DBRS reconfirming on 16 January 2026, general government debt of 37.6% of GDP on the rating-agency measure, a constitutional debt brake, an estimated fiscal surplus of 0.4% of GDP and effectively no Confederation supply story. The transmission is specific: a widening 10-year differential that comes from a fiscal risk premium rather than a policy signal carries no quote-currency-positive content, so a weak 30-year auction or a bad budget headline is pair-positive even though it widens the yield gap against the franc. Confidence is 58 because the deterioration is partly discounted in the JGB market already.

Each further 100bp of Japanese tightening adds roughly JPY 5trn, close to 0.9% of GDP, to the debt-service line - the assumed rate has already moved 3.0% to 3.8% and added JPY 5.36trn in a single budget cycle - at the same time as the BoJ steps its JGB purchases down from JPY 2.5trn a month to JPY 2.1trn by Q1 2027, so supply rises as the dominant buyer withdraws. The transmission is a slow allocator preference that must be expressed in the currency rather than the bond, because the Swiss bond offers no yield to express it in, and it is one of the two factors that stop this pair's strategic score being more negative. tactical.score_interpretation: A net score of -0.0502 sits well inside the neutral band of -0.10 to +0.10, so the derived tactical stance is Neutral. The composition is far more interesting than the number: this is not ten indifferent factors but two opposing blocs that nearly cancel. Against the pair, Policy & Rates contributes -0.1488, Guidance -0.0630 and Market Structure -0.0260, a gross -0.2378. For the pair, Inflation & Growth contributes +0.0990, External Balance +0.0480, and Fiscal & Sovereign +0.0406, a gross +0.1876. Four factors score zero - Risk Appetite, Flows, Event Risk and USD Liquidity - and in each case the zero is a genuine two-sided assessment.
tactical.rationale: At the applied tactical weights this pair is decided by two blocs that very nearly cancel, and the honest verdict is that there is no four-week direction here. The bearish bloc is dated and mechanical: the franc pays 100bp less than the yen today, the Bank of Japan is 80-90% priced to take that to 125bp on 18 September, and the Swiss National Bank meets six days later with a conditional inflation forecast explicitly conditioned on a 0.00% rate through 2028, so the differential can only move one way inside the window. Guidance reinforces it rather than adding independent information - the SNB has told the market twice since June that it has an increased willingness to intervene against rapid franc appreciation while the BoJ's Summary of Opinions says its hiking pace will be faster than market expectations - and the only observable option skew in the pair, the quote leg's -1.74 volatility points at one month, points the same way. Between them those factors carry -0.2378 of weighted score. The bullish bloc is undated but real. Switzerland has produced the strongest surprise run in years, with Q2 GDP at +1.5% quarter-on-quarter against a +0.2% to +0.4% consensus, KOF at a four-and-a-half-year high and industrial production beating by 10.2 points, while Japan's Q2 grew 0.3% with no contribution from consumption; Switzerland posted its largest trade surplus since 1950 in the same month Japan's trade deficit widened 4.1-fold on a fuel bill up 53.5% year-on-year; and the sovereign-quality gap between AAA at 37.6% debt-to-GDP and A-band at 214.5% with a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line is the widest in the G10. Those carry +0.1876. The base and quote dossiers reinforce each other in the bearish direction - a standalone Bearish CHF view and a standalone Bullish JPY view both imply a falling cross - and the reason this verdict is less bearish than that naive combination is precisely bilateral: the two factors each dossier treats as its own currency's structural strength, external balance and sovereign quality, happen to be the two on which Switzerland dominates Japan most decisively, and they are what stop the score clearing -0.10. What is priced is the September hike and the September hold; what is not priced is the Japanese terminal, where the curve implies about 1.21% after December against a surveyed consensus of 1.75%, and that residual is the single clearest edge, running against the pair. The path of least resistance is therefore a mild drift lower punctuated by the dated repricing points rather than any four-week trend. The catalyst sequence is dense: the 3 September 30-year JGB auction, Japanese CPI on 17 September, the BoJ on 18 September, the SNB on 24 September, the Swiss referendum on 27 September and the coincident 30 September US funding deadline and Japanese interim fiscal close. Conviction is 2 because the score is small, because more than half the bearish contribution rests on one decision that is already discounted, and because a short position in this cross is paid only 126.9bp a year to wait - enough to make the strategic expression economic, not enough to make a four-week one compelling.
tactical.g10_relative_ranking: Among franc crosses, CHF/JPY is the one where the base leg's carry deficit is smallest - 100bp against the yen versus 435bp against the Australian dollar, 425bp against the krone and 375bp against sterling - so it is the least punitive place to be long the franc and the least rewarding place to be short it. Among yen crosses it is the mirror image and more attractive: it is the only long-yen expression in the G10 with positive carry, roughly +126.9bp annualised, against -335bp for AUD/JPY and -275bp for GBP/JPY, and both legs are havens so the risk-regime beta that makes AUD/JPY and NZD/JPY punishing largely cancels. On this cycle's standalone scores the franc ranked ninth of eleven tactically and the yen fourth, which places CHF/JPY among the better-quality short candidates in the yen complex on fundamentals even though its four-week signal here is flat. The pair also now carries an explicit sell-side endorsement that its peers do not: investors are turning to franc funding to sidestep the risk of Japanese intervention, making short CHF/JPY an attractive carry-positive way to express a bearish yen view.

strategic.rationale: Over one to six months this becomes a contest between the monetary-policy block and the structural block, and the policy block wins by 0.0708 of weighted score. On one side, Policy & Rates retains its 0.24 weight and Guidance rises to 0.13, so a franc pinned at 0.00% with a conditional forecast conditioned on that rate through 2028, against a Bank of Japan whose published Summary of Opinions says the pace of hikes will be faster than market expectations and whose curve implies only about 1.21% by December against a surveyed terminal of 1.75%, contributes -0.2520. The differential compresses against the base leg through a sequence of dated events - the 30 October Outlook Report, which is the projection round most capable of moving the path, and the 18 December decision - while the SNB assessments on 24 September and 10 December can only restate the status quo. On the other side, External Balance at 0.16 and Fiscal & Sovereign at a raised 0.10 contribute +0.1812: a Swiss current account of 9.77% of GDP and a net international investment position of CHF 974bn against a Japanese surplus that is 27.6 times primary income rather than trade, with the goods account in deficit, terms of trade down from 90.5 to 81.62 in two quarters, a net creditor rank slipped to third and a reserve share down 0.40 percentage points in a quarter; plus AAA at 37.6% debt-to-GDP against A-band at 214.5% with a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line at a 3.8% assumed rate. Those two blocs interact rather than merely summing, and the interaction is the most important thing in this verdict: the same Japanese tightening that makes Factor 1 bearish for the pair costs roughly JPY 5trn of debt service per 100bp and therefore makes Factor 8 bullish for it, which is precisely why the quote leg has not been rewarded for a thirty-year high in its own yields. Base and quote dossier views reinforce each other downward - Bearish CHF plus Bullish JPY - and our score is less negative than that combination because the bilateral lens puts Switzerland's two structural advantages against Japan's two structural weaknesses in the same pair. What is priced is captured in a cross-derivation from named leg forecasts, USD/CHF 0.78-0.79 and USD/JPY around 154-157, which implies the franc appreciating against the yen; we take the other side of that, less because of the modal path than because the terminal-rate gap and the official-flow asymmetry are unpriced. The path of least resistance is a slow, contested franc depreciation against the yen, most likely front-loaded into the autumn policy window and vulnerable to a reversal if energy falls. Dated catalysts are the BoJ on 18 September, 30 October and 18 December, the SNB on 24 September and 10 December, the Japanese FY2027 draft budget in late December and the 31 December funding turn. Conviction is 2 rather than 3 because the score clears the threshold by only 0.03, because the largest bullish factor depends on an oil price nobody can forecast, and because the carry, at 126.9bp a year in favour of a short position, is small enough that the call must be right on direction rather than merely paid to wait.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically CHF/JPY is one of the more attractive shorts in the franc complex and the cleanest long-yen expression in the G10. Among franc crosses it is the only one where the base leg faces a counterpart central bank that is actively tightening while its own is pinned, so the differential deteriorates rather than merely being wide, unlike CHF/SEK or the 425-435bp gaps to NOK and AUD that are static and already extreme. Among yen crosses it is the only one paying positive carry to the long-yen side, roughly 126.9bp annualised, and it pairs a hiking central bank against a zero-rate one with both legs classified as havens, so it captures the yen view without the risk-proxy beta of AUD/JPY or NZD/JPY. On this cycle's standalone strategic scores the yen ranked third of eleven and the franc sixth, which is consistent with a modest bearish tilt in the cross rather than a high-conviction one. The competing franc-short expressions are where the rotation is currently most visible, and those pairs offer positive carry to the franc-short side rather than the modest 126.9bp available here, which is the honest case for preferring them if the view is franc-negative rather than yen-positive.

Meanwhile External Balance doubles in weight from 0.08 to 0.16 and Fiscal rises from 0.07 to 0.10, so the structural block holds roughly constant at +0.1812 against +0.1876 while the policy block grows from -0.2378 to -0.2520. In plain terms: over four weeks the pair is held up by an unpriced Swiss data run that has no strategic durability, and once that is removed the monetary-policy block wins.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Late October to December 2026, specifically the 30 October BoJ Outlook Report (the projection round most capable of repricing the Japanese path) and secondarily the 18 December decision; working the other way, Swiss Q4 data should begin to show the tariff front-running reversing over the same window.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the four-week verdict as flat and the one-to-six-month verdict as a modest downward tilt whose economics do not depend on a fast move, because a short is paid roughly 20 pips a month. The strategic position should be built on rallies into 194.50-197.50 rather than at spot, and the informational content of the call sits after the 30 October Outlook Report rather than before the 18 September decision.

forward_vs_spot.edge_6m: +565 pips (+2.91%) short-side edge versus forward, though the six-month point is extrapolated beyond the observed 13.6-104.7 day roll window and is the least reliable of the three

catalysts.rationale: The cleanest near-term test of whether the Japanese long-end sell-off is a policy repricing or a fiscal risk premium. The 28 August 2-year auction drew a bid-to-cover of 2.97 against a twelve-month average of 3.74 and the 25s30s spread is inverted at -1.0bp. A weak tail confirms the fiscal channel, which is quote-negative and therefore pair-positive despite widening the yield gap; a strong auction lets the policy channel dominate and is pair-negative.

July payrolls printed -23,000 with 103,000 of downward revisions, and the market has since moved to price a September Fed hike at roughly 57.5%. A second weak print questions that hike and is risk-negative, which in a haven-versus-haven pair favours the leg with the larger short and the official bid beneath it - the yen. A strong rebound sustains the carry regime that is currently eroding both legs, with no clean cross direction.

July printed 1.9% headline and 1.8% core with the BoJ's own ex-special-factors measure at 2.3%, and government energy subsidies are suppressing the headline by roughly 40-50bp. Against a Swiss core of 0.4% the inflation differential is already about -140bp; a core print at or above 2.0% would make the 18 September hike a certainty and push the terminal higher, compressing the bilateral differential further against the base leg.

July produced the largest Swiss surplus since the series began in 1950, on exports up 13.8% with chemicals and pharmaceuticals up 25.7%. A second consecutive large surplus would force the balance-of-payments story into a pair narrative dominated by carry, which is base-positive; a sharp fall would confirm July as Section 232 front-running and would weaken the heaviest positive factor in the strategic score.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision
catalysts.rationale: The largest single dated event in the tactical window and the mechanical driver of the bilateral differential: a 25bp move to 1.25% takes the CHF-JPY policy gap from -100bp to -125bp with no Swiss offset available at any point in the horizon. Roughly 80-90% is priced, so the tradeable content is the accompanying language - whether the Board repeats the Summary of Opinions formulation about a pace faster than market expectations, which would reprice the terminal and the pair together.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment
catalysts.rationale: A hold at 0.00% is effectively certain, so the entire content is in the language and the refreshed forecast, and the hot August print raises the stakes. Softening or dropping the anti-appreciation sentence would be read as tolerance of a stronger franc and is pair-positive; retaining and hardening it caps the base leg in any risk event and is pair-negative.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality
catalysts.rationale: Passage would bar Switzerland from joining sanctions against belligerent states absent a UN Security Council mandate, forcing a re-examination of the framework under which Russian-linked assets are frozen in Switzerland, and cutting both ways for the franc's haven premium. Polling of roughly 62% against makes rejection the strong base case; the pair's own volatility term structure charges nothing for the roughly 20% passage tail.

catalysts.event: US FY2027 appropriations deadline and Japanese interim fiscal half-year close
catalysts.rationale: Two coincident events with the same sign for this cross. A US shutdown is precedented and would be risk-negative, which in a haven-versus-haven pair favours the leg with the larger speculative short and the official bid beneath it. Separately the Japanese interim book close generates documented repatriation and dividend flows that hit spot yen, and life-insurer hedge ratios at historic lows mean a higher share reaches spot rather than rolling off forwards.

The first test of whether the August acceleration to 0.8% headline and 0.4% core is petrol-driven noise or the start of a trend. Core annual inflation rose only slightly in August, and it is the more important metric the SNB looks at more closely, so a second core rise to 0.5-0.6% would be the genuine signal and would begin pulling first-hike pricing forward from June 2027. That is the cleanest identifiable route to invalidating the strategic Bearish call.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan decision with quarterly Outlook Report
catalysts.rationale: The highest-stakes date in the window because it is a projection round: the July Outlook already revised FY2027 core CPI up to 2.4% and described CPI risks as skewed to the upside, and the October revision incorporates a terms-of-trade shock and the energy-subsidy unwind. This is the identified inflection point for the pair - the event most capable of taking the Japanese terminal above the roughly 1.21% the curve implies for December.

The point after which the US political incentive to participate in yen-supportive intervention weakens. The July joint operation was partly motivated by the link between yen volatility and US borrowing costs ahead of the vote; once past, the standing joint commitment that currently underpins the quote leg becomes less credible at the margin, which removes an official bid from beneath the pair.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment
catalysts.rationale: The final SNB assessment of 2026 and the last opportunity inside the strategic window for the base leg's policy stance to change. A hold at 0.00% is all but certain, so the variables are the intervention language and any revision to the 2027-2028 forecast path, now more interesting given August ran marginally above the Q3 conditional forecast.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting decision
catalysts.rationale: The single largest gap between guidance and pricing in the pair: OIS implies a Japanese policy rate of only about 1.21% after this meeting, meaning a second 2026 hike is lightly priced, while half of 36 surveyed economists name 1.75% as terminal and 35 of 54 expect at least 1.50% by end-March 2027. A move here would widen the bilateral differential to -150bp and would be a genuine repricing rather than a confirmation, with no Swiss offset possible.

catalysts.event: Japan FY2027 draft budget Cabinet approval (week-dated on the FY2026 precedent)
catalysts.rationale: The event that decides whether the fiscal channel or the policy channel dominates the quote leg into 2027. Ministry requests total roughly JPY 143trn with a record JPY 36.6trn debt-service line on a 3.8% assumed rate, against a stated new-issuance cap of about JPY 40trn versus JPY 29.6trn in the FY2026 initial budget. A breach of the cap converts more of the JGB yield rise into pure risk premium, which is quote-negative and pair-positive; containment is pair-negative.

The largest recurring dollar-funding squeeze in the calendar and the most reliable seasonal source of cross-currency basis widening. Because both legs of this cross are funding currencies, a basis widening forces both to be bought back and offers no clean direction; the asymmetry, if any, is that the yen carries the larger identified speculative short and the two named yen-basis channels could amplify the effect on that leg specifically.

invalidators.condition: Swiss core CPI prints at or above 0.6% year-on-year for two consecutive months and the swaps curve pulls the first SNB hike into the first half of 2027 from its current June 2027
invalidators.mechanism: The entire strategic Bearish case rests on Factor 1's premise that the base leg is pinned with a tight, near-symmetric distribution while only the quote leg has a path - a Swiss hiking path inside or adjacent to the horizon converts a -100bp differential that only widens into one that can narrow, and the strategic score's 0.030 margin does not survive the loss of even a third of Factor 1's -0.1584.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Swiss core CPI (currently 0.4%) and SNB first-hike date on the swaps curve (currently June 2027)
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly for CPI, daily for the curve

invalidators.condition: The Bank of Japan holds at 1.00% on 18 September without language committing to a near-term move
invalidators.mechanism: 80-90% of a hike is priced, so a hold is a 25bp surprise delivered straight into the heaviest factor in the pair, and it would be read as the Board yielding to fiscal pressure from a JPY 36.6trn debt-service line - which simultaneously converts Factor 8 from a background pair-positive into the dominant driver.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: BoJ Statement on Monetary Policy and the 2-year JGB (currently 1.743%)

invalidators.condition: Brent crude sustains below USD 80 for four consecutive weeks and Japan's terms-of-trade index recovers above 86 from 81.62
invalidators.mechanism: External Balance is the largest single positive contribution on either horizon at +0.1152, and its entire content is a terms-of-trade transfer that was almost purely price rather than volume - crude import value rose 87.8% on volume up 5.5% - so a price reversal repairs it faster than it accrued and removes roughly two thirds of the structural block that currently offsets the policy block.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Brent front month and the Japanese monthly corporate goods price index terms-of-trade series
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily for Brent, monthly for the index

invalidators.condition: CHF/JPY closes above 199.64 on a weekly basis, clearing the three-touch 198.4864-199.63869 band and reclaiming both the 100-day at 200.18161 and the 200-day at 199.73433
invalidators.mechanism: That band is the only structure between spot and the four-touch 203.15-203.98 zone, it contains both longer moving averages, and reclaiming it would mean the market has read the entire September-October policy sequence as pair-positive - which is only coherent if the base leg's rate story has repriced.

invalidators.condition: The CFTC franc net short extends beyond -40,000 contracts while the yen combined net short covers to better than -50,000
invalidators.mechanism: The funding rotation would then be complete rather than in progress: the pair-negative flow asymmetry that Factor 4 scores depends on the yen carrying the larger latent short, and a crossover means the franc has become the crowded leg and the squeeze risk has changed sides.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Commitments of Traders, franc all-speculator net (currently -19,900) and yen leveraged-fund plus asset-manager net (currently -97,158)
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly, Friday release for the prior Tuesday

invalidators.condition: The Japanese 30-year JGB rises above 4.50% from 4.092% while CHF/JPY simultaneously rises above 196.80
invalidators.mechanism: That specific combination is the definitive proof that Japanese yields are rising on fiscal risk premium rather than policy expectation - in a policy-driven repricing the quote leg strengthens as yields rise, so if both rise together the differential argument carrying Factor 1's -0.1584 stops transmitting to this cross at all.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Ministry of Finance daily compound yields, 30-year, paired with CHF/JPY spot

invalidators.condition: CHF/JPY 20-day realised volatility rises above 12% from 7.78% while the pair falls more than 5% in a month
invalidators.new_stance: Bearish (tactical, from Neutral) with conviction raised
invalidators.mechanism: The 126.9bp annualised carry that currently makes both funding trades viable becomes uneconomic on a risk-adjusted basis at that volatility - the short-side carry-to-vol ratio falls from +0.16 to +0.11 - and a disorderly move would trigger the SNB's stated willingness to intervene against franc appreciation, the wrong direction to help a falling cross.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: 20-day realised volatility from the price store and one-month CHF/JPY implied where obtainable

signposts.confirms_if: Widens beyond +150bp, consistent with the BoJ delivering on 18 September and the residual basis holding
signposts.invalidates_if: Narrows below +100bp, meaning either the differential or the basis has moved against a short position
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only number that tells you what a rolled position in this pair actually pays, as opposed to what the two policy rates imply. At 20 pips a month it is the reason a short CHF/JPY expression does not require a fast move, and it is the single most pair-specific datum in the report.
signposts.frequency: Daily, from the gated store's derived carry file

signposts.indicator: Bilateral policy rate differential (SNB minus BoJ)
signposts.confirms_if: Reaches -125bp on 18 September and December OIS pricing for the BoJ moves above 1.40%
signposts.invalidates_if: The BoJ holds on 18 September, or Swiss swaps price a first SNB hike inside the first half of 2027
signposts.bilateral_importance: The yen is the only G10 currency that pays the franc a positive policy carry, so this is the one franc cross where the differential runs against the base leg rather than for it - a 25bp change here is proportionally far more significant than the same change on a 435bp AUD/CHF gap.
signposts.frequency: Quarterly for the SNB (24 September, 10 December), eight times a year for the BoJ (18 September, 30 October, 18 December)

signposts.indicator: Swiss core CPI versus Japanese core CPI
signposts.current_level: Swiss core 0.4% year-on-year (August 2026) against Japanese core 1.8% (July 2026) - a differential of -140bp
signposts.confirms_if: Japanese core reaches 2.0% or above while Swiss core holds at or below 0.4%, widening the gap beyond -160bp
signposts.invalidates_if: Swiss core reaches 0.6% for two consecutive months, which would begin pulling the SNB's first hike into the horizon
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the widest core inflation differential in the G10 and the only channel through which the base leg's policy distribution can change inside the horizon. Core is the metric the SNB looks at more closely to decide on monetary policy.
signposts.frequency: Monthly - Swiss on the first business days, Japanese national on the third Friday

signposts.indicator: Brent crude and Japan's monthly mineral fuel import bill
signposts.current_level: Brent in the low 90s; Japanese July mineral fuel imports JPY 2,680.4bn, 22.1% of all imports, up 53.5% year-on-year; terms of trade 81.62 from 90.5 in Q1
signposts.confirms_if: Brent falls below USD 80 with the terms-of-trade index recovering above 86 - note this invalidates the pair-positive Factor 5 and therefore confirms the bearish cross thesis
signposts.invalidates_if: Brent sustains above USD 105 on Hormuz escalation with a Japanese monthly trade deficit wider than JPY 900bn
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the cleanest asymmetry in the pair. Both economies import energy, but Japan imports essentially all of its hydrocarbons at 22.1% of total imports while Switzerland's exposure is a fraction of that relative to output, and Switzerland has an offsetting gold correlate that Japan lacks.
signposts.frequency: Brent daily; Japanese trade statistics monthly

signposts.indicator: CFTC franc net short versus yen combined net short
signposts.current_level: Franc all-speculator net -19,900 contracts (2026-08-28 release, 48th percentile of one year); yen leveraged funds plus asset managers -97,158 (2026-08-25 report, 33rd percentile of ten years)
signposts.confirms_if: The franc short extends beyond -30,000 while the yen short covers to better than -60,000, confirming the rotation in position data rather than commentary
signposts.invalidates_if: The franc short extends beyond -40,000 while the yen short covers past -50,000, at which point the franc is the crowded leg and squeeze risk has changed sides
signposts.bilateral_importance: For a cross, only the relative position matters - both legs short simultaneously mutes the signal, which is why Factor 4 is tactically Neutral. The convergence between the two is the specific thing the rotation narrative predicts.
signposts.frequency: Weekly, Friday release for the prior Tuesday

signposts.indicator: USD/JPY one-month 25-delta risk reversal (skew proxy for the pair)
signposts.current_level: -1.74 volatility points, yen calls bid, 5.4 times the EUR/USD equivalent of -0.32; decaying to -1.46 at three months, -0.91 at six and -0.16 at one year
signposts.confirms_if: Stays beyond -1.50 at one month, indicating professional hedgers continue to pay for the yen tail that is the pair's left tail
signposts.invalidates_if: Less negative than -1.00, meaning the market has stopped paying for yen upside and the only observable skew in the cross has flattened
signposts.bilateral_importance: No CHF/JPY risk reversal and no franc risk reversal could be sourced this cycle, so this is the only observable skew bearing on the pair, and it belongs entirely to the quote leg.

signposts.indicator: CHF/JPY spot versus the 198.4864-199.63869 three-touch band and the 50d/200d cross
signposts.current_level: Spot 192.92537, 614 pips and 3.18% below the band midpoint; 50-day 198.51478 now below the 200-day 199.73433
signposts.confirms_if: Spot stays below 196.80 and the 50-day continues to fall away from the 200-day, with a weekly close below 190.00
signposts.invalidates_if: A weekly close above 199.64 reclaims the three-touch band and both longer averages
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the pair's own structure and it is the only place in this report where the chart is admissible evidence. The asymmetry - four resistance bands within 5.52% overhead against a 1368-pip air pocket to the first support - means the shape of the risk in this cross is directional even when the fundamental score is not.
signposts.frequency: Daily, weekly close for the invalidation threshold

assumptions: This is pass 2 of a two-pass process. The ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions and factor rationales are carried verbatim from pass 1, which scored them without the price payload; nothing has been re-scored.

The payload delivered 130 weekday bars covering 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, with spot 192.92537 at spotDate 2026-09-03. Moving averages, zones, 52-week statistics and 200-week figures are computed over the whole stored history (2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03, 4,879 weekday bars), not just the 130 bars shown.

The valuation date is 2026-09-01 and the payload's spotDate is 2026-09-03 - the price anchor postdates the valuation date by two trading sessions, which contained a 446-pip, 2.31% decline. Both dossiers were built to a 2026-08-28 price tail and quote CHF/JPY at 197.815; that figure is not used anywhere for levels in this report.
The base dossier records CHF/JPY 60-day realised volatility at 6.64% and a one-year gain of +7.17%; the payload gives 7.31% and +3.57% respectively. The payload governs for all price-derived metrics.

CHF/JPY has no listed option, so the payload's ATM implied volatility figures are a triangle-and-realised-correlation construction using an implied correlation of 0.5971, documented as understating direct Eurex quotes by a median 14.4% across seventeen tested pairs. Every use in this report treats the figure as a floor. No CHF/JPY or franc 25-delta risk reversal could be sourced; the quote leg's USD/JPY skew is used as the only observable proxy and labelled as such.

The 126.9bp annualised funding premium is the gated store's CME calendar-spread cross (6S/6J, observed 2026-08-31, 13.6 to 104.7 days). By covered interest parity it is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis and cannot be decomposed without an OIS curve; it is not the policy differential. Forward outrights are model derivations on an actual/365 basis, not dealer quotes, and the six-month point is extrapolated beyond the observed roll window and is the least reliable of the three.

Policy rates are SNB 0.00% and BoJ 1.00%, both as of 2026-09-01, differential -100bp. The 10-year yields are monthly series as of 2026-06-01 and are used only for cross-currency spread comparability, labelled monthly at every occurrence.

Bilateral trade figures are taken directly from the supplied IMF DOTS structured block for 2024 and not re-estimated from the web; the mirrored Japanese figures in the same block differ, which is normal for bilateral statistics, and the Swiss-reported net is relied upon.

CFTC positioning dates are not contemporaneous: the franc aggregate is the 2026-08-28 release with detail from an 11 August tranche; the yen figures are the 2026-08-25 report. The 'both legs short' conclusion is robust to that, but precise percentiles are not directly comparable.

Each dossier's own inline caveats are inherited rather than repaired, including the unverified Swiss reserve-publication date, the unverified Swiss trade-balance calendar value, the uncited IMF Japanese debt and deficit series, the unresolved US tariff rate on Japanese autos, and the estimated Japanese REER percentile of 2. No fair-value level is asserted for this cross - the REER comparison is a relative-gap construction, not a PPP calculation.

Post-dossier developments (Swiss August CPI, the acceleration in Swiss quarterly growth, the swaps-implied June 2027 first SNB hike, and the CME-implied 57.5% September Fed hike probability) are incorporated in the narrative, pass-2 factor notes, catalysts, invalidators and signposts, but have not been used to alter any factor stance or confidence.

Five factors were adjusted from default weights, all justified bilaterally and all within +/-0.05, summing to exactly 1.00 on both horizons: Risk Appetite (tactical only, cut), External Balance (tactical only, raised), Guidance & Credibility (both horizons, raised), Fiscal & Sovereign Risk (both horizons, raised), and USD Liquidity & Funding (both horizons, cut).

No CHF/JPY bank research forecast exists and none is invented; the consensus discussion uses a labelled cross-derivation from named leg forecasts plus discretionary pair commentary, and explicitly identifies algorithmic extrapolation sites as non-research whose 174-to-225 dispersion is itself evidence they carry no information.

No options expression is specified because the pair has no listed option and its surface cannot be priced from the data available. Scenario probabilities and invalidator probabilities are analyst judgements calibrated to the factor analysis, not options-implied.
